thread:
maria: Quick sync — we need a crisp rule for who makes tenant routing + eviction decisions across hosted / dedicated / private. Ambiguity is causing race conditions during failover.

arjun: +1. proposal summary: control plane owns routing for hosted; for private, the local agent owns routing and eviction; for dedicated, control plane owns policy but agent holds a short-lived lease token so we can avoid split-brain.

ben: Concrete risk: if dedicated runtime loses control-plane connectivity for ~30s, control plane might evict and reschedule while runtime keeps serving -> duplicate work and billing confusion. We need TTL + clear revoke semantics.

sasha: Sketch for a minimal "lease" API that should reduce races. Agent obtains a lease, control plane can revoke. Basic endpoints:
```
POST /leases    { tenant_id, runtime_id, ttl_seconds } -> { lease_id, expires_at }
GET  /leases/{id} -> { holder, expires_at, state }
POST /leases/{id}/revoke -> 200
```
If agent has valid lease, it may continue serving despite transient control-plane unavailability. Revoke forces graceful shutdown window.

maria: Love the simplicity. Also we should return routing hints alongside decisions so callers know preferred fallbacks. Example envelope: 
```
{ "route": "prefer-local", "fallbacks": ["dedicated-standby","hosted-burst"], "hint_ttl": 10 }
```
This lets SDKs and routers implement short-term sticky preferences.

ben: Add a "defer" codepath: when control plane cannot assert a winner, it returns 202 + "defer-to-holder" with lease_id. That way the agent that currently holds lease continues until expiry. Avoids hard evict on noisy network.

sasha: We should also publish audit events for: lease_granted, lease_revoked, lease_expired, route_assigned, route_fallback_used. Ops needs them for postmortem.

elaine: Ops question: who stores the secrets needed to validate lease tokens, especially for Private where customers run their own control plane? KMS? local certs? Need a short bootstrap doc.

arjun: For private: the customer's control plane issues signed short-lived tokens; agent validates locally using customer's public certs rotated via the trust anchor. For dedicated/hosted: our control plane issues tokens and agents validate using platform certs. Keep TTL short (eg 15s-120s) to limit blast radius.

maria: Action items:
- sasha: draft RFC for lease API + routing-hint envelope (include error codes and example flows).
- ben: enumerate failure modes + eviction race matrix and suggested mitigations.
- elaine: write bootstrap note for secret/cert distribution for private agents.
Sync end-of-week? :calendar:

ben: will watch canary and report perf/latency. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the single source for RFC follow-up and followups. Feel free to ping me if you need more context.
